tools_found.tool_name: Internal AI code generation (Google monorepo / Cider, reported in Pichai earnings stat)
tools_found.signal_summary: Google's CEO has repeatedly disclosed on earnings calls a rising share of new code at Google that is AI-generated (then reviewed by engineers), starting at >25% in Q3 2024. This reflects internal dogfooding of Google's own Gemini-powered tooling.

evidence.claim: Sundar Pichai stated on the Q3 2024 earnings call that more than a quarter of all new code at Google is generated by AI, then reviewed and accepted by engineers.
evidence.quote: Today, more than a quarter of all new code at Google is generated by AI, then reviewed and accepted by engineers.

evidence.claim: Reported follow-on figures: >30% by Q1 2025, ~50% by late 2025, and ~75% by Q2 2026 of new code AI-generated and engineer-approved.
Q3 2024 stat reported with engineer-review context; corroborated by multiple outlets.
Alphabet Q3 2025 earnings 8-K is the primary filing context for the most recent earnings-call statements.

tools_found.signal_summary: Cider is Google's internal Gemini-powered IDE (tightly integrated with Critique, Google's code review tool); it provides AI autocomplete, AI-suggested changelist descriptions, AI code-review input and a chat interface. Critique offers one-click ML-powered edit suggestions on review comments.

evidence.claim: Cider is Google's in-house code editor tightly integrated with Critique; Critique shows ML-powered suggested edits that the author can apply with one click, and 97% of Google engineers report satisfaction with Critique.
Google engineers must use in-house tools such as Cider and Gemini for Google (formerly Goose); Cider suggests changelist descriptions, gives AI input on code reviews, and offers AI autocomplete.

tools_found.tool_name: Goose / Gemini for Google (internal on-machine AI agent)
tools_found.signal_summary: Goose (later branded 'Gemini for Google') is Google's internal Gemini-powered coding assistant trained on Google's engineering knowledge, used to accelerate internal product development. Engineers are reportedly mandated to use it over third-party tools.

evidence.claim: Google developed Goose, a coding assistant leveraging Gemini and built on Google's ~25-year engineering knowledge base, to accelerate internal product development.

Google reportedly mandates internal AI tools (Cider, Gemini for Google / formerly Goose) and prohibits unapproved third-party AI coding tools; managers reportedly ask engineers to demonstrate daily AI usage.

tools_found.signal_summary: Google's open-source (Apache 2.0) terminal AI agent launched June 25, 2025, bringing Gemini into the command line for refactoring, docs generation, shell command execution and file editing, with MCP support.

evidence.claim: Google announced Gemini CLI, an open-source AI agent for the terminal, on June 25, 2025, under Apache 2.0 with free tier (60 req/min, 1000/day) and MCP support.
Gemini CLI launch coverage confirming open-source terminal agent positioning.

tools_found.signal_summary: Google's agentic development platform / IDE (a modified VS Code fork) launched Nov 18, 2025 alongside Gemini 3; orchestrates multiple parallel autonomous agents and supports multiple models including Anthropic's Claude Sonnet/Opus and an OpenAI open variant. Antigravity 2.0 (I/O 2026) expanded it to IDE + CLI + SDK + Managed Agents.

evidence.claim: Google launched Antigravity, an agentic development platform, with the Gemini 3 release; it is a modified VS Code fork orchestrating up to 5 parallel agents.
Antigravity supports multiple AI models including Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Claude Opus 4.6 and an open-source OpenAI variant (GPT-OSS-120B); launched Nov 18, 2025.
Antigravity 2.0 announced at I/O 2026 (May 19), expanding to desktop IDE, CLI, SDK, and a Managed Agents tier in the Gemini API.

tools_found.signal_summary: Google's asynchronous, autonomous coding agent (Gemini 2.5 Pro) that clones repos into a cloud VM, plans, makes multi-file changes, runs tests and opens GitHub pull requests. Public beta May 2025; general availability Aug 6, 2025.

evidence.claim: Jules is Google's autonomous coding agent; official Google Labs product page/blog.

Jules exited public beta to general availability on Aug 6, 2025 with deeper GitHub integration (auto-opening PRs), environment snapshots and Gemini 2.5 thinking mode; ~2.28M beta site visits and 140k+ publicly shared code improvements during beta.

tools_found.signal_summary: Google's commercial AI code assistant (VS Code, JetBrains, GitHub app), generally available for individuals and GitHub, powered by Gemini 2.5, with an agent mode and a code review agent. A product Google sells; also reflects Google's own tooling lineage.

evidence.claim: Gemini Code Assist for individuals and GitHub is generally available, powered by Gemini 2.5, with a code review agent via the GitHub app; updates announced at Google I/O 2025.
Google reported a controlled experiment finding Gemini Code Assist boosted developers' odds of completing common dev tasks by 2.5x vs no assistance.

tools_found.signal_summary: DeepMind's Gemini-powered evolutionary coding agent that autonomously discovers and optimizes algorithms; deployed internally across Google's compute ecosystem (Borg scheduling, TPU design, kernel/FlashAttention optimization), recovering ~0.7% of worldwide compute on average.

evidence.claim: AlphaEvolve discovered a heuristic improving Borg data-center orchestration that on average continuously recovers ~0.7% of Google's worldwide compute; also improved kernel tiling (23%) and FlashAttention (32%) and helped design next-gen TPUs.
AlphaEvolve technical paper describing the coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery.

tools_found.tool_name: Third-party agentic tools (Claude, OpenAI models) usable inside Google products, not internal default
tools_found.signal_summary: Google's own Antigravity platform exposes third-party models (Anthropic Claude Sonnet/Opus, an OpenAI open variant) as selectable options for external developers via BYO API key. Internally, Google engineers are reportedly restricted to in-house tools, so third-party agentic coding tool dogfooding inside Google was NOT evidenced.

evidence.claim: Antigravity lets external developers route to Anthropic Claude (Sonnet 4.6 / Opus 4.6) via their own Anthropic API key; this is a product option, not internal Google engineering usage.

notes: Evidence is rich. Primary sources: Google/DeepMind blogs (Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Jules, AlphaEvolve, Gemini Code Assist) and Alphabet SEC 8-K filings for earnings context. Exec quote (Pichai >25% new code AI-generated, Q3 2024) is widely and consistently reported. CAVEAT on AI-code-% figures: only the Q3 2024 >25% figure is a clean directly-attributable Pichai quote in these results; the 30%/50%/75% follow-ons are reported by secondary outlets / social posts and should be treated as directional/lower-confidence. CAVEAT on internal mandate: the 'engineers must use internal tools / third-party prohibited' claim comes from secondary tech-press (TechRadar, SightsInPlus) reporting on leaked internal guidance, not a Google primary source. NAME-COLLISION CAVEAT: Google's internal 'Goose' assistant is distinct from Block's open-source 'Goose' agent (donated to Linux Foundation Dec 2025); search results conflated them, so the Goose details are lower confidence. WebFetch was broadly blocked (HTTP 403) in this environment, so claims rely on WebSearch result summaries; all source_urls are real URLs that appeared in search results. No evidence found that Google ENGINEERS internally use third-party agentic tools (Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code, Codex) as a default — reporting indicates the opposite. Did not run a job-posting-specific search beyond the policy reporting.
